findings.description: The replacement validation accepts multiple JSON documents and null, although the ledger requires exactly one object.
findings.failure_mode: Input such as '{} {}' passes `jq empty` and timestamp stamping produces two objects that can overwrite the ledger. Likewise, `null` becomes an object containing only last_updated, allowing an invalid update to replace ledger state.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the single-object validation using `printf '%s' "$content" | jq -es 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")'`.

findings.description: Unconditionally skipping heredoc bodies excludes executable shell code from the swallowed-jq check.
findings.failure_mode: A script containing `bash <<'EOF'` followed by `jq ... || echo fallback` now passes the check. An unquoted heredoc containing `$(jq ... || echo fallback)` also passes even though the shell executes that substitution.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain executable-heredoc detection and scan interpreter-fed bodies and expansions in unquoted heredocs while skipping literal fixture bodies.

findings.description: The simplified regex mistakes here-strings and quoted text for heredoc declarations.
findings.failure_mode: For `value=$(cat <<<'x: 1')`, the regex matches `<<'x` within the here-string and sets the terminator to x. Without a subsequent standalone x, every remaining line is skipped, including real swallowed-jq violations. A quoted string containing `<<WORD` causes the same failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore here-string exclusion and quote-awareness before recognizing heredoc declarations.

findings.description: Removing the ValueError handler leaves embedded NUL characters in review content unhandled by the adapter.
findings.failure_mode: The prompt is passed directly on argv, so a message containing a NUL makes subprocess creation raise ValueError before agy starts. This bypasses ProviderUnavailableError handling and aborts completion instead of advancing to the fallback provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore conversion of subprocess ValueError into ProviderUnavailableError, preserving fallback behavior for prompts that cannot be transported on argv.

findings.description: The guard was weakened from `jq -es 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")'` to `jq empty`. `jq empty` exits 0 for any well-formed JSON stream: the literal `null`, a multi-document stream (`{...}\n{...}`), arrays, and scalars. Two of those now reach the stamping step and are written: (a) `null` — `null | .last_updated = $ts` yields `{"last_updated":"..."}`, so a caller that produced `null` (e.g. `jq '.missing_key' file`) replaces the entire ledger with a one-key stub while returning success; (b) a multi-document stream is stamped per document and written as concatenated JSON, which single-document readers (`jq -e '.x' ledger`) then misparse. This is the same failure class as bug 20260808-a008c6 that the removed check was added to close. Arrays/scalars are still caught only incidentally because the stamping jq errors and the `-z "$updated_content"` check fires.
findings.failure_mode: A caller passes `null` or a multi-doc JSON string; the ledger is backed up, locked, and overwritten with a stub or a multi-document file, and every caller reports success. Ledger state is silently lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the strict shape check: `printf '%s' "$content" | jq -es 'length == 1 and (.[0] | type == "object")' >/dev/null 2>&1` (or at minimum `jq -e 'type == "object"'` combined with a single-document check). Keep the error message mentioning non-object content.

findings.description: `printf '%s' "$content"` was replaced with `echo "$content"` on both the guard and the stamping pipeline. With `shopt -s xpg_echo` (or bash invoked as `sh` on hosts built with xpg echo default), `echo` interprets backslash escapes, so JSON string content such as `"\\n"` (escaped backslash-n) is rewritten to `"\n"` before jq sees it. That is still valid JSON and so passes the guard, but the stored value has changed. Escapes that produce invalid JSON (`\u`, bare `\n` inside strings) would at least fail the guard.
findings.failure_mode: Under xpg_echo semantics, backslash sequences inside ledger string values are silently altered on every write; under default bash the change is a no-op, so the risk is environment-dependent.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert to `printf '%s' "$content"` in both places; there is no benefit to `echo` here and `printf` is the project convention the original code used.

findings.description: The rewritten `_start_heredoc` dropped three pre-filters: stripping here-strings (`<<<...`), stripping arithmetic (`$(( ))`/`(( ))`), and the quote-balance check on the prefix. The remaining regex `<<-?[[:space:]]*['"]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*['"]?` matches starting at the second `<` of a here-string: for `<<<'x: 1'` it matches `<<'x` and sets `hd_term="x"`, `in_heredoc=1`. Likewise `<<WORD` inside a string literal (e.g. `echo "use <<EOF here"`) now opens a heredoc. Because the terminator line never arrives, the `in_heredoc { ... next }` rule swallows every remaining line of the file, so no `jq ... || echo` after that point is ever reported.
findings.failure_mode: Any script containing a here-string with a leading-alpha word (reviewer cites run-preflight.sh:83 `<<<'x: 1'`) or a `<<WORD` in a string literal silences the scanner for the rest of that file. The CI gate passes on code it was built to reject, with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinstate the pre-processing on a scratch copy of the line before matching: remove `<<<` here-strings (`gsub(/<<<[[:space:]]*("[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^[:space:]]+)/, "", scan)`), remove `$(( ))`/`(( ))`, and skip the match when the prefix has an odd count of `'` or `"`.

findings.description: Removing `hd_exec` (and `_hd_command`/`INTERP`) makes every heredoc body unconditionally skipped. The old logic only skipped bodies that were genuinely inert; it still scanned bodies that execute: (a) heredocs piped to an interpreter (`bash <<'EOF'`, `python3 <<'EOF'`, `cat <<'EOF' | bash`), and (b) heredocs with an unquoted terminator (`cat <<EOF`), where `$(jq ... || echo ...)` inside the body is expanded and executed by the enclosing shell. Both are real `jq || echo` sites and both are now invisible to the scanner. The new comment frames all heredoc content as 'fixture/documentation text', which is not true for these two shapes.
findings.failure_mode: Swallowed jq errors inside executable heredocs pass the CI check. The reviewer measured five existing sites lost in .claude/scripts (anthropic-oracle.sh:300, beads/loa-prime.sh:33-35, run-preflight.sh:237), so this is a confirmed regression of the tool's contract, not a theoretical one.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore `hd_exec` computation in `_start_heredoc` (quoted-terminator check plus interpreter detection via `_hd_command` and the trailing `| bash`-style pipe test) and keep the `if (hd_exec) { ... _line_has_swallowed_jq ... }` branch in the `in_heredoc` rule. If the goal is only to skip bats fixture heredocs, scope the skip to quoted-terminator heredocs whose command is `cat`/`printf`/`run`/a variable assignment.

findings.description: The suppression-marker rule changed from `{ _start_heredoc($0); next }` to `{ next }`. A line such as `cat <<'EOF' # check-no-swallowed-jq: ok` is now skipped without entering heredoc state, so the fixture body that follows is scanned as ordinary shell. Planted bad examples (`jq ... || echo ...` lines in bats fixtures) are then reported, which is exactly the false positive the Step 1 comment says the heredoc skip exists to prevent. Combined with DISS-003, the body may also open a phantom heredoc from its own content.
findings.failure_mode: CI fails on bats tests or docs that put the suppression marker on a heredoc opener line; the suppression no longer suppresses the body.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `_start_heredoc($0)` in the marker rule: `/#[^\n]*check-no-swallowed-jq:[[:space:]]*ok/ { _start_heredoc($0); next }`.

findings.cross_file_justification: headless_cli.py:418 retains `except (OSError, ValueError)` for the sibling CLIs, and tests/test_agy_headless_adapter.py::test_nul_byte_prompt_walks_not_crashes pins that an embedded-NUL prompt raises ProviderUnavailableError. The dispatcher in cheval.py maps unknown exceptions to API_ERROR and stops the chain rather than walking.
findings.description: The `except ValueError` clause around `run_subprocess_pgkill` was deleted. agy is argv-transport: the entire flattened prompt (untrusted review content) is passed as a single argv element. If it contains a NUL byte, `subprocess.Popen` raises `ValueError('embedded null byte')`, which is not an `OSError` subclass and so is not caught by the remaining `except OSError` branch. The ValueError now propagates out of `complete()` uncaught. Every other failure in this block (timeout, output cap, FileNotFound, E2BIG) is mapped to a typed cheval error so the fallback chain can advance; this one path now crashes instead.
findings.failure_mode: A review payload containing a NUL (binary hunk, corrupted diff, pasted file) makes the gemini-headless terminal raise a raw ValueError. cheval.py's catch-all returns API_ERROR and does not fall through to gemini-api, so the review fails outright rather than degrading. The existing test `test_nul_byte_prompt_walks_not_crashes` will fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the clause: `except ValueError as exc: raise ProviderUnavailableError(self.provider, f"agy -p got un-execable argv (embedded NUL in the prompt?): {exc}") from exc`, or fold it into the OSError branch as `except (OSError, ValueError)` to match headless_cli.py:418.
